results.content:
Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version. It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.

That’s an impressive showing compared to previous robotic AI systems, but it’s still probably not enough for a company like Mercedes-Benz. A human doing that sort of repetitive task will get it right virtually every time, and DeepMind director Kanishka Rao notes that closing that last 4 percent gap will be a “steep road.” [...] Argon was also used for analyzing failures and suggesting ways to improve in both simulations and real robots. However, this isn’t something that works in real time. Frontier models like Gemini take time to churn through their tokens, but robots need to be able to operate without long pauses. The new VLA isn’t lightning quick, either. While Google has experimented with some embedded robotics models, the current 2.5 release is still running on cloud-based servers. So those gains in accuracy and speed still don’t come without latency. The video above is sped up by 2x to make the robot look more human-like. [...] DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate.

# Google DeepMind Releases Gemini Robotics 2.5

By Brian Heater, Managing Editor, A3

11/10/2026

3 minutes

Google DeepMind just unveiled Gemini Robotics 2.5, in conjunction with the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) in Austin this week. The latest version of the  vision-language-action (VLA) has been tested across 200 distinct tasks, per the division.

Updates include more robust dexterity, safety improvements, and a reliability metric of “96% success rate,” with Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid during proof-of-concept trials on Mercedes-Benz lines at German and Hungarian factories.

results.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5 Puts Apollo 2 on Mercedes-Benz Lines as Argon Speeds Up Training | Humanoids Daily
results.content:
Written byPontus Armini

 Google DeepMind has released Gemini Robotics 2.5, a vision-language-action model that it says succeeds 30% to 100% more often than Gemini Robotics 2 across more than 200 tasks, and finishes them 20% to 30% faster.
 In a proof of concept on active Mercedes-Benz lines in Kecskemét, Hungary, and Sindelfingen, Germany, Apptronik's Apollo 2 used the model to sort metal brackets from bulk bins into sequencing trays with a 96% success rate.
 DeepMind credits Gemini 4 Argon for the four-month turnaround. Argon ran thousands of practice attempts in simulation and reviewed replays of the robot's failures to adjust training recipes.
 The model is rolling out to DeepMind's robotics partners only. Google has not announced API access, pricing, or new ER or On-Device versions. [...] ## Task-by-task gains over Gemini Robotics 2

DeepMind compared the two VLA generations on a Franka FR3 Duo with two-fingered parallel grippers and on Apollo 2 with SharpaWave hands, in four categories: tabletop pick-and-place, multi-step and contact-rich tasks, precision kitting and insertion, and dexterous manipulation. Across the set, Gemini Robotics 2.5 succeeded 30% to 100% more often, depending on the task type, and completed tasks 20% to 30% faster.

Most of the published examples are tasks Gemini Robotics 2 could not do at all: [...] | Task | Gemini Robotics 2 | Gemini Robotics 2.5 |
 --- 
| Pack pastries with tongs | 5% | 100% |
| Close the lid of a toolbox | 0% | 93% |
| Untie a ribbon bow | 0% | 70% |
| Hang a cardigan | 0% | 62% |
| Sweep trash into a dustpan with a brush | 0% | 52% |
| Pack a rice cooker | 0% | 40% |
| Fold pants | 0% | 40% |
| Unhang a mug and place it on a table | 29% | 75% |

On tabletop pick-and-place, DeepMind says the new model reached 100% on many tasks where its predecessor scored far lower or zero, but it did not publish per-task figures for that category or for kitting and insertion. The post does not give the number of trials behind each percentage. Other examples in the announcement include tying a bow on a gift box and pipetting liquid.

# Gemini Robotics 2.5 accelerates real-world general dexterity

Carolina Parada

We’re enabling robots to learn faster for the real world - from everyday skills to the factory floor  
  
Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Earlier this year, we brought whole-body intelligence to robots of many types, including humanoids. Now, in large part thanks to Gemini 4 Argon's ability to accelerate robotics research, we have further pushed the frontier of physical intelligence. We tested Gemini Robotics 2.5’s capabilities in task breadth, performance, and complexity across over 200 distinct tasks, though this approach could scale to many more.

Gemini Robotics 2.5 marks a leap forward in three key areas:
